research_question: At KBTP high-activity terminal windows, can causal current-state features provide calibrated probabilistic predictions of future proximity-event counts at 30, 120, and 300 seconds across unseen dates, and does a low-capacity overdispersed count model improve on Ridge without adding a new deep architecture?
claim_boundary: Proximity-event proxy forecasting at KBTP; not controller workload, official separation violation, accident risk, or universal airspace complexity.
input_condition: The same eight current, prediction-time-observable control features for all primary model families.

model_families.configuration: StandardScaler + Ridge(alpha=1.0), trained separately per horizon

StandardScaler + PoissonRegressor; alpha in [0.01, 0.1, 1.0, 10.0] selected once per horizon on original validation days by equal-day mean NB2 negative log likelihood; NB2 dispersion estimated on original train rows only
HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss='poisson', max_iter=100, max_leaf_nodes=15, learning_rate=0.05, l2_regularization=1.0, random_state=1701); no tuning

supplemental_model.restriction: Existing checkpoints were trained only for 120 seconds; A is not evaluated as a 30- or 300-second model and is not eligible to determine the primary route.

risk_definition.method: training-set 75th percentile with numpy higher quantile

distribution.dispersion_estimation: training-only method of moments, clipped to at least 1e-8

metrics.probability_primary: Brier score for the frozen high-risk event
metrics.uncertainty: paired day bootstrap with 10000 resamples and exact two-sided sign test

evaluation_sets.development: original train and validation dates only
evaluation_sets.retrospective: original four test dates plus the already observed round-1 and round-2 external dates; descriptive, never used for gate selection
evaluation_sets.confirmation: exactly one mechanically selected round-3 batch of eight unseen dates, excluding all original and prior external dates

horizon_success_gate: On the round-3 confirmation days, poisson_nb2_controls has lower equal-day mean count MAE than ridge_log1p_controls and wins at least five of eight days.
On the same days, poisson_nb2_controls has lower equal-day mean Brier score than the frozen training-prevalence probability baseline and wins at least five of eight days.
The aggregate 90% NB2 interval coverage is between 0.80 and 0.98 inclusive, and aggregate 10-bin ECE is at most 0.10.
route_success_gate: At least two of the three horizons must pass every horizon-level gate.
stop_conditions: If fewer than two horizons pass, stop probability-model development, retain Ridge as the final primary model, and frame the study as a cross-date benchmark/negative result.
If at least two horizons pass, proceed once to the second-airport low-capacity calibration experiment.
Regardless of outcome, do not add another KBTP confirmation batch, new neural architecture, new high-interaction threshold, or new hyperparameter search.
